title: The second pledge
hookLine: seventy-three men and two women pledge to protect him as their own

cards: Another pilgrimage. Another night at Aqaba. But this time it's after dark, a third of the night gone, and people are slipping away from their sleeping companions one or two at a time, creeping like birds, Ibn Ishaq says.

They gather in a ravine: seventy-three men and two women, by his count. One of the women is Nusayba bint Ka'b, known as Umm Umara. They've come to make a different kind of promise than the twelve made a year before.

teach.h: AL-ABBAS: PROTECT HIM OR LEAVE HIM.
teach.b: The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, comes with his uncle al-Abbas, who, Ibn Ishaq says, still followed the religion of his people but came to look after his nephew. Al-Abbas speaks first, and bluntly.
He is safe among his own clan. If you're going to take him, be sure you can protect him. If not, leave him now.

The Prophet recites the Qur'an to them and asks for their pledge: that they protect him as they protect their own women and children. Al-Bara ibn Ma'rur takes his hand and says yes: we are people of war and weapons.
Then Abu al-Haytham raises a hard question. We have ties with other people in Yathrib, and we'll be cutting them.
If we do this, and God gives you victory, will you go back to your own people and leave us? The story says the Prophet smiled and answered: no. Blood is blood.
I am of you and you are of me.

teach.h: I AM OF YOU, YOU ARE OF ME.
teach.b: I will fight whom you fight, and make peace with whom you make peace. See what's changed. The first pledge was about conduct.
This one is about bodies and homes: we will stand in front of you.
And it runs both ways; they ask for his loyalty as clearly as he asks for theirs. Their reward, he tells them, is paradise. In the story, no wealth is promised, and no power.

how: Muslims remember the second pledge of Aqaba as the promise that opened the way to Medina, and honor the Ansar, the helpers of Medina, for keeping it.

games.q: you're Abu al-Haytham. you're about to cut ties at home for this man. what do you ask him?
o: will you leave us once you win?
games.why: he asked if the Prophet would go back to his own people. he smiled: I am of you and you are of me.

practice: Bring to mind the people you already protect without thinking: a child, a parent, a friend.

Then widen it by one, someone exposed right now with nobody standing in front of them, a coworker who gets talked over, a neighbor living alone, and hold them there for a moment. If you pray, you can ask God to keep them safe.

wordCard.voice: Aqaba. The ravine where, at night, seventy-three men and two women of Yathrib pledged to protect the Prophet as their own families, and he pledged he was theirs. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: protect him as your own. A promise that ran both ways. See you tomorrow.
